summary: This is a configuration file that sets up environment variables for running a Joomla content management system in Docker. It specifies database credentials, admin account details, service versions, and port mappings needed to launch the application.

explanations.1: CONTAINER_PREFIX is a naming convention used to identify Docker containers related to this Joomla installation.
explanations.2: DB_NAME sets the name of the MySQL database that Joomla will use to store its content and configuration.
explanations.3: DB_PASSWORD is the password for the database user account — it should be changed from this example to something secure in production.
explanations.4: DB_USER is the username that Joomla will use to connect to and access the MySQL database.
explanations.6: JOOMLA_ADMIN_EMAIL is the email address for the Joomla administrator account, used for notifications and password recovery.
explanations.8: JOOMLA_ADMIN_PASSWORD is the password for logging into Joomla's admin panel — like DB_PASSWORD, this example should be replaced with a real secure password.
explanations.10: JOOMLA_ADMIN_USER is the display name for the admin account that will appear in the Joomla interface.
explanations.12: JOOMLA_ADMIN_USERNAME is the actual login username (different from the display name) used to sign into Joomla's admin panel.
explanations.14: JOOMLA_SITE_NAME is the title of the website that will display to visitors.
explanations.15: JOOMLA_VERSION specifies which version of Joomla to install and which PHP and Apache versions it should run with.
explanations.16: MYSQL_PORT is the network port number where the MySQL database service will listen for connections.
explanations.17: MYSQL_VERSION specifies which version of MySQL to download and run in Docker.
explanations.19: WEB_PORT is the port number on your computer where you'll access Joomla in your web browser (like localhost:8080).
